newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/yen ends firmer in U.S. after setting new high.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen ends firmer in U.S. after setting new high.

text.p: Dollar/yen ended higher amid talk a report concluded the U.S. government wants a stronger dollar and a growing perception Japan is unsure how to contend with the sliding yen, experts said.
The dollar reached a high of 119.80 yen, its highest level in 47 months.
"Just hearing rumors to that effect is enough to make the market move," said Frank Pusateri, a vice president at Mellon Bank in Boston. "But I wouldn't put much stock in it."
"All I can say is it is a continuation of the trend there, just bucking to take out 120 (yen)," Pusateri added.
The dollar continued past its high in Tokyo to peak at 119.80 yen in the U.S., despite vague rumors the Bank of Japan had tried to stem its rise.
The dollar ended at 119.20/25 yen, up slightly from 119.15/20 yen at the open. It fell to 1.6321/26 marks from 1.6400/10.
Traders said a newsletter from a Washington consultancy was the catalyst for the dollar's leg higher.
The consultants reportedly said recent market rumors that the U.S. Treasury Department targeted an exchange rate of 140 yen per dollar were not entirely off base.
The report also raised questions as to how Japanese authorities will react to further dollar appreciation.

Japanese officials have repeatedly warned against excessive weakness or strength in the yen since the Japanese stock market commenced a sharp decline at the beginning of the year. A senior Ministry of Finance official reiterated this enjoinder on Thursday.

"The market, not seeing any Bank of Japan (BOJ) intervention and not hearing of verbal intervention overnight, was probably a little more confident trying it higher," said Dennis Pettit, manager of foreign exchange at Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan.
"They are clearly concerned about the BOJ doing something but it's not at all obvious that we've seen anything from them yet." Pettit said.
Against the mark, however, a dollar advance failed to exceed 1.6455, a 31-month high first reached on Wednesday.
Dollar/mark weakened after the Bundesbank failed to lower rates, which supported the mark for most of the session, traders said.
Recently, traders have been selling marks, partly because many thought the Bundesbank might loosen credit to stimulate Germany's faltering economy.

"People had been short marks. The Bundesbank did nothing this morning on the interest rate side, so I think people began to take some of those positions back," said John Nelson, a senior vice president at ABN-AMRO Bank in Chicago.
Elsewhere, the dollar closed at 1.4155/65 Swiss francs, down from 1.4260/70 francs at the open.
The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3445/50 from C$1.3388/93.
The pound fell to $1.6295/05 from $1.6310/20, and the Australian dollar rose to $0.7717/22 from $0.7714/19.
((-Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
